data.description:
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior (review-loop divergence observed during waxen-sigma merge-to-main)

#### Expected Behavior
A change's diff converges to a stable review verdict in a bounded number of cycles (review.max_cycles=4).

#### Actual Behavior
The two-channel staged release reviews essentially the same cumulative diff twice — review-sub-pr on work->staged AND llm-review on staged->main — plus independent CodeRabbit + Gitar checks. Across the waxen-sigma session each fix sub-PR re-triggered fresh reviews surfacing NEW false-positive / nitpick / stale findings with no convergence: e.g. a STALE 'line 99 word-split' finding posted after the fix already used a bash array; an FP 'git option injection' despite the 'git add --' separator; an FP 'output format change' that was a no-op (already space-joined); markdownlint MD040 + single-quote-escaping edge nits. Clearing required TWO separate /dso:fp-recovery opus passes (#550 and #548, each 0 critical/important/fragile). This is FP amplification across the two-channel boundary + cross-bot stacking, defeating the cycle cap. Related future work already noted in FP-RECOVERY-WORKFLOW.md: swap-maple-flyby (cycle-end arbiter) and side-pane-tithe (FP-rate measurement); this ticket tracks the specific two-channel double-review amplification.
data.title: CI llm-review: two-channel double-reviews same diff (review-sub-pr + llm-review) -> FP amplification, non-converging review cycles
